headline: 7,500 Bangladeshis held in Saudi prisons, says State Minister
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam revealed the figure during a press briefing at the airport after receiving the body of a citizen killed in a missile strike.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam announced that approximately 7,500 Bangladeshis are currently detained in prisons across Saudi Arabia.

The revelation came during a press briefing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, where she was receiving the body of Mohammad Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi national killed in a missile strike in Saudi Arabia.
The government is currently coordinating with Saudi authorities to extend visas and iqamas for expatriates who are unable to return to their workplaces due to ongoing conflict.
Additionally, the government is discussing the rehabilitation and re-employment of Bangladeshi citizens who have lost their jobs abroad.
Regarding the recent execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia, the State Minister stated that the government has yet to receive detailed information about the cases.
Bangladesh has formally requested copies of the verdicts from Saudi authorities to establish the facts of these executions.
Shama Obaed emphasized that while Bangladesh cannot interfere in another country's judicial system, it remains responsible for obtaining information and assisting its citizens.
The government continues its efforts to gather further information regarding the cases of detained nationals.

Additionally, the government is discussing the rehabilitation and re-employment of Bangladeshi citizens who have lost their jobs abroad.

Regarding the recent execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia, the State Minister stated that the government has yet to receive detailed information about the cases.

Bangladesh has formally requested copies of the verdicts from Saudi authorities to establish the facts of these executions.

Shama Obaed emphasized that while Bangladesh cannot interfere in another country's judicial system, it remains responsible for obtaining information and assisting its citizens.

headline_marked: Green shift: [[Vegetable gardens take root]] on Dhaka’s landfill
headline: Green shift: Vegetable gardens take root on Dhaka’s landfill
summary: Urban farming is transforming waste disposal sites into productive green spaces, providing food and livelihoods for local residents.
details: Urban farming is transforming Dhaka's landfills, turning waste disposal sites into productive vegetable gardens. This initiative is helping to recover land and reclaim the environment.
Local residents and farmers are utilizing the organic waste and composted soil of the landfills to grow a variety of vegetables, turning a once-polluted area into a green zone.
The project aims to reduce the city's dependence on on external food sources and promote sustainable urban agriculture within the city limits.
Beyond food production, these gardens are helping to mitigate the environmental impact of landfills by improving soil quality and absorbing carbon dioxide.
Experts suggest that if scaled up, this model of urban farming on landfills could provide a sustainable solution for waste management and food security in densely populated cities.
